data.claim: Yes: services/ask verdict() trusts the folded log, so a hand-appended ask.answered with human=true is an approved verdict, even for an ask that was minted with a one-time code (coded is self-reported). Only the engine's answer() refuses agents.
data.falsifier: verdict() returns ok=False for an ask.answered appended through EventLog.append without going through answer().
data.mechanism: The fold (core/handlers/asks.py) does not authenticate writers; answer()'s agent refusal is a call-site check, and the log is plain files the agent can append to.
data.probe: scratchpad p.py: request an ask with_code, answer() as an agent (refused), then log.append('ask.answered', ... human=True); verdict()
data.probe_output: agent answer -> refusing: answering is a person's act ...; verdict before forge: False; verdict after hand-appended event: Verdict(ok=True, reason='cmd:gate.skip:X:critic approved by operator')
data.question: Can a same-uid agent obtain an approval the ask engine accepts without a person, by appending the event itself?

evidence.note: ddflow research add (CONFIRMED): hand-appended ask.answered is accepted by verdict(); output in the research record. Inventory of refusal sites and ask engine read.

data.body: New package ddflow/services/approvals/. sites.py declares one row per verb (gate.skip.failed_review, grant.add, approve.partial, reviewers.approve, chore.approve, export.ack, config.reviewer_command, upgrade.self, plan.confirm, claim.force, complete.force, skew.override) with tier T1/T2/T3, default min level, which state is digested. data.body: Per D-RA-1/2. canon.py builds the canonical JSON and digest from verb, args, item, gate, requesting agent, reason and the acted-on state (reuse gate_accept.digest). request.py files the ask (subject cmd:<verb>:..., uses, min level) and renders the operator text. Adds [approvals] ttl_s, use_ttl_s, auto_request, default tiers. Event ask.requested gains fields; ask.consumed event kind registered (event registry). Agents may request and read, never answer. (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)
data.title: Pending approval request: canonical command record, state digest, ddflow-rendered text, requester binding, expiry and uses on the ask engine; [approvals] knobs

data.body: The MVP core. operator_gate(verb, params, caller, approval_id): person at terminal as today; agent with an approval recomputes the digest from current state, checks requester, expiry, uses, level, spends one use under the log lock (ask.consumed) and stamps the effect with human, proxy, ask id, level, channel; otherwise refuses naming the route and (auto_request) files the ask. Sites: approval.grant, grants.add, reviewer_trust, gate_accept, api/chore, api/gates failed-review skip, export ack/disable/enable. Also fixes the verdict trusting self-reported human/coded (research Finding 1) for levels above L1. Shared --approval flag helper. (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)
data.title: Single-use hash-bound approval check in every refusal site: operator_gate() replaces the bare agent_marker refusal; --approval ID; verdict re-verifies proof

data.body: approve/deny/revoke are person-only (resolve_actor; ANSWER_SOURCES), show the rendered text and digest and require the person to confirm; request/list/show/withdraw are open to agents. approve takes --signature/--code later channels plug in. Exemption entry for the answer verbs (no MCP action). (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)

data.body: Per D-RA-4. Ships examples OFF: review_round up to 5 when the tree changed after triage; skip of a gate whose reviewer was unavailable 3 times; accept measured baseline-red partial. Policy answers are ask.answered by=policy:<id>, policy=true, human=false; consumed only for verbs that allow policy. Company floors only tighten; an agent surface cannot write [approvals]. data.body: approvals show --sign-payload prints the payload (namespace ddflow-approval; ask id, digest, outcome, expiry); approve --signature verifies and records the answer; the agent may courier it. ddflow never creates or stores a key (D-CM-7). Falls back to the commit allowed-signers file. If ssh-keygen is missing the channel is unavailable, never passed. Related: CM-sign (no hard edge). (research docs/ddflow/research/remote-approvals.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/remote-approvals.md)
data.title: Signed approvals (L4): ssh-keygen -Y sign/verify over the canonical payload against [approvals].signers, verified offline; shares the signer list with CM-sign
